g11-economics-ue3-t1.overview: Nature and Importance of National Income Accounting sits inside National Income Accounting. National income accounting is the focus of Unit 3 of Grade 11 Economics in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it explains the nature and importance of national income accounting. Then it defines GDP and GNP. Next, it measures national income three ways: the expenditure, income, and value-added approaches. Also it weighs the problems of GDP measurement and separates real GDP from nominal GDP. Finally, it covers other income measures and income distribution. Students will also learn how national income accounting tracks real-life economic performance.
objectives: Explain the nature and importance of national income accounting.
Define GDP and GNP.
Compute national income by the expenditure, income, and value-added approaches.
Distinguish nominal GDP from real GDP.
Calculate the GDP deflator and the consumer price index.
g11-economics-ue3-t1.simple:
Nature and Importance of National Income Accounting in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the national income account as the record of a country’s output and income.
  • Also why governments and economists rely on it.
g11-economics-ue3-t1.detailed:
Nature and Importance of National Income Accounting — the essentials. First, the national income account as the record of a country’s output and income. Also why governments and economists rely on it.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Explain the nature and importance of national income accounting.
  • Define GDP and GNP.
  • Compute national income by the expenditure, income, and value-added approaches.
  • Distinguish nominal GDP from real GDP.
  • Calculate the GDP deflator and the consumer price index.
